title: Survival Analysis of Time-to-Detection for Control Protocols

original_idea.body:
# Survival Analysis of Time-to-Detection for Control Protocols

**Problem:** Protocols are compared by final safety score, but two with the same score can differ in how quickly they catch sabotage, and many trajectories are censored.

**Direction:** Import survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier, Cox, right-censoring). Treat steps-until-detection as a survival time with censored never-caught cases, and compare protocols via survival curves and hazard ratios on replayed trajectories.

**Why it matters:** A principled, censoring-aware way to compare detection speed, crucial when early detection prevents irreversible harm. Pure statistics, no compute.

**Relevant context:** Kaplan-Meier/Cox; Ctrl-Z (arXiv:2504.10374); arXiv:2511.02997.
